questions.question: What is the N+1 query problem and how do you fix it in Rails?
questions.title: N+1 Query Intro
questions.direct_answer: N+1: you fetch N records, then trigger 1 query PER record for an association, instead of 1 query for all. `User.all.each { |u| u.posts.count }` runs 1 query for users, then 1 PER user for posts count = N+1 queries. With 100 users that's 101 queries instead of 2. Fix: eager-load with `includes` — `User.all.includes(:posts)` loads posts in 1-2 queries (a JOIN or a second IN query) for ALL users. Detect N+1: the bullet gem warns in dev/test, or watch the log for many identical queries in a loop. Variants: `preload` (2 queries, no join — good when you don't filter on the association), `eager_load` (a JOIN — when you WHERE on the association), `includes` (Rails picks). For counts alone, counter caches (`posts_count`) avoid the query. The cost of N+1: many small queries are far slower than one batched query, especially over the network. Rule: if you loop and touch an association, eager-load it.

sections.title: N+1
sections.content:
1 query per record for an association (N+1 total). Fix with includes/preload/eager_load. Detect with bullet.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User.all] --> E[each: u.posts.count]
  E --> Q1[q1: users] --> QN[q2..qN: posts per user]
  QN --> X[N+1 queries]
  I[User.all.includes(:posts)] --> B[1-2 queries]
  B --> Y[fast]
```

sections.title: N+1 query
sections.content:
```ruby
# N+1: fetch N records, then 1 query PER record for an association
users = User.all                      # 1 query (users)
users.each { |u| puts u.posts.count }  # 1 query PER user (posts)  -> N+1
# 100 users -> 101 queries (slow).

# FIX: eager-load with `includes`
users = User.all.includes(:posts)      # 1-2 queries total (JOIN or IN)
users.each { |u| puts u.posts.size }   # posts already loaded; no extra queries

# Variants of eager loading:
#   preload      -> 2 queries (users, then posts WHERE user_id IN (...))
#                  good when you DON'T filter on the association
#   eager_load   -> a JOIN (1 query) -- when you WHERE on the association
#   includes     -> Rails picks (preload usually; eager_load if you WHERE on it)
User.preload(:posts)                   # 2 queries
User.eager_load(:posts).where(posts: {published: true})  # JOIN
User.includes(:posts).where(posts: {published: true})   # Rails -> JOIN

# Detect N+1:
#   - 'bullet' gem warns in dev/test (logs N+1)
#   - watch the log: many identical queries in a loop = N+1

# For counts alone, use a COUNTER CACHE (no query at all):
#   belongs_to :user, counter_cache: true
#   user.posts_count  # stored on user; no COUNT(*) query

# Cost: N small queries >> 1 batched query (network round-trips).
# Rule: if you loop and touch an association, EAGER-LOAD it.
User.all.includes(:posts, :comments).each { ... }   # multiple associations
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Looping over records and touching an association without includes (N+1).
Using includes when you want a specific strategy (preload/eager_load are explicit).
Counting associations in a loop without a counter cache (N+1 COUNTs).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: N+1 = fetching N records then 1 query per record for an association (N+1 total).
Fix: eager-load with includes/preload/eager_load (loads all in 1-2 queries).
preload = 2 queries (no join); eager_load = JOIN; includes = Rails picks.
Detect N+1 with the bullet gem or by watching the log for many identical queries.
For counts, use a counter cache (posts_count); rule: loop + association => eager-load.
